questions.title: Why does FlashAttention‑3 use a circular on‑chip buffer instead of a simple shared‑memory staging buffer?
questions.question_body: In Algorithm 3.1 the authors describe a circular SMEM buffer with an $s$‑stage pipeline and then a warp‑specialized layout. I understand the goal is to hide memory‑load latency, but I’m not exactly sure how the circular buffer improves concurrency over a normal double‑buffer on warp‑group level. Can someone explain the contention points that this design eliminates?

questions.title: How does the ping‑pong scheduling actually overlap softmax and WGMMA in practice?
questions.question_body: The paper claims that by splitting warp‑groups into producers and consumers and using `bar.sync` one can have softmax calculations of one block executed while another block’s GEMM is running. Since softmax uses a multiplicative exponential kernel, how are its arithmetic operations mapped to the multiple SMs? Does this result in costly traffic between register files of different warps, or is it entirely in‑SM?

questions.title: What are the register pressure implications of the 2‑stage WGMMA–softmax pipeline?
questions.question_body: The authors mention that we have to keep an extra $	extbf{S}_{	ext{next}}$ in registers. For a typical configuration (e.g., $B_r=64$, $B_c=64$, head dimension 128) how many register bytes does this add? Does this limit the achievable block size or lead to spilling on H100?

questions.title: Why is FP8 WGMMA only k‑major while FP16 accepts mn‑major and k‑major?
questions.question_body: Section 3.3 talks about layout constraints for FP8 WGMMA – specifically that it can only take k‑major inputs. What is the hardware reason for this restriction? Does it stem from cache line organization, vector length, or something else?

questions.title: How do you perform an in‐kernel transpose of 8‑bit tiles using LDSM/STSM?
questions.question_body: The text describes transposing tiles of $	extbf{V}$ after loading them into SMEM via `ldmatrix`/`stmatrix`. Since these instructions deal with an 8×8 matrix of 16‑bit entries, how do we pack two 8‑bit values per word and still get a correct transpose? Do we need extra shuffles or byte permutes to unpack?

questions.title: "Block quantization" vs. "per-tensor scaling" for FP8 attention
questions.question_body: I understand per-tensor scaling multiplies all elements in $	extbf{Q}$ by a single scalar before quantization. The paper proposes keeping one scalar per block (e.g., per $B_r 	imes d$ tile). How does this affect the subsequent linearity of $	extbf{Q}	extbf{K}^T$? Does scaling each block separately change the relative magnitudes across queries in a way that hurts attention’s temperature?

questions.title: How does incoherent processing with a random orthogonal matrix improve FP8 numerical accuracy?
questions.question_body: "Incoherent processing" multiplies $	extbf{Q}$ and $	extbf{K}$ by an orthogonal matrix $	extbf{M}$ before quantization. Intuitively I see that $(	extbf{Q}	extbf{M})(	extbf{K}	extbf{M})^T = 	extbf{Q}	extbf{K}^T$, but why does this help reduce quantization error? Is it because outliers get spread out among more elements?

questions.title: Why is FP8 FlashAttention‐3 slower for small sequence lengths with causal masking?
questions.question_body:
The ablation study shows that for causal masking at short seq.
lengths FP8 FlashAttention‐3 underperforms cuDNN H100 kernels. Is this due to lack of persistent kernel design, or are there additional reasons such as increased register pressure or pipelining overhead when very few blocks are processed?

questions.title: "Rounding errors” in softmax when using FP16-$	o$FP32 rescaling
questions.question_body: The forward pass keeps intermediate softmax results in FP32 but outputs in FP16/FP8. Since we subtract rowmax and exponentiate, could rounding errors accumulated in FP32 cause significant coefficient changes when downcasted back? How do we guarantee numerical stability across large values of $N$?

questions.title: "Three-stage pipelining" – when would it actually pay off?
questions.question_body: Section 3.2 mentions a theoretical extension to three stages, overlapping more operations. In an H100 environment with 4 warp groups per CTA and a block size of 128x128, would adding another stage overcome the extra register pressure? What empirical tests should I run to decide if it's worth it?

questions.title:
"Cache friendliness” of contiguous vs.
non-contiguous accesses in WarpSpecialization
questions.question_body: "Producer warps" load $	extbf{K}_j,	extbf{V}_j$ from global memory into shared memory while "consumer warps" read them back for GEMM. Are there any benefits to reordering these accesses so that key/value tiles are contiguous across material batches? Would reordering improve TMA efficiency or just cause more strided loads?
